## Abstract

This project investigates how tuition, financial aid indicators, and institutional characteristics relate to student retention and post-graduation earnings 
using the U.S. College Scorecard dataset. After filtering the data to bachelor’s-degree-granting institutions and performing extensive preprocessing, exploratory 
analysis revealed substantial variation in cost, student composition, and outcomes across institutions. Linear and Ridge regression models were used to estimate 
relationships with median earnings ten years after enrollment, while logistic regression and random forest classifiers predicted whether an institution fell above 
the national median earnings level. Results show that retention, completion rates, tuition, institutional size, and Pell Grant share are among the strongest predictors 
of outcomes. These findings highlight the combined influence of cost, socioeconomic composition, and institutional performance on long-term student success.
